title: Comparison of GMI, PNF, and Standard Care for Post-Traumatic Elbow Stiffness Rehabilitation in Adults
official: Open-label Randomized Interventional Study Comparing the Efficacy of Graded Motor Imagery (GMI) and Proprioceptive Neuromuscular Facilitation (PNF) Protocols With Standard Care in the Rehabilitation of Post-traumatic Elbow Stiffness in Adults.
summary:
TRICEPS is a single-center, randomized, open-label, three-arm study evaluating two rehabilitation approaches for post-traumatic elbow stiffness in adults: Graded Motor Imagery (GMI) and Proprioceptive Neuromuscular Facilitation (PNF), each combined with standard care, compared with standard care alone.

A total of 75 adults aged 18 to 64 years with post-traumatic elbow stiffness following a fracture will be randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio to one of three groups: standard rehabilitation alone, standard rehabilitation combined with GMI, or standard rehabilitation combined with PNF. The treatment period will last 6 weeks.

The primary objective is to compare the effects of these rehabilitation approaches on upper-limb functional capacity, assessed using the Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand (DASH) score at baseline and after 6 weeks of treatment. Secondary outcomes include muscle strength, active joint range of motion, pain, kinesiophobia, and health-related quality of life.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults aged 18 to 64 years
* Post-traumatic elbow stiffness following an elbow fracture treated surgically or non-surgically
* Enrollment 6 to 8 weeks after the initial management of the elbow trauma
* Elbow stiffness defined by at least one of the following limitations : flexion less than 130°, extension deficit greater than 30° (extension range less than - 30° as specified in the protocol), supination less than 50°, or pronation less than 50°
* Limitation of elbow flexion and/or extension in the sagittal plane
* Written, free, informed, and explicit consent to participate in the study
* Beneficiary of the French social security system or eligible as a dependent, excluding beneficiaries covered by State Medical Aid (AME)

Exclusion Criteria:

* Infection of the surgical wound
* Unhealed fracture
* Complex regional pain syndrome
* Peripheral nerve injury
* Lesion requiring further surgery, such as an osteoma or ankylosis
* Cognitive impairment preventing the patient from understanding the information provided about the study
* Limited joint mobility or absence of the contralateral upper limb
* Psychiatric, visual, rheumatological, or neurological condition that could compromise the rehabilitation treatment
* Under legal guardianship, curatorship, or judicial protection
* Detained or deprived of liberty by judicial or administrative decision
* Beneficiary of State Medical Aid (Aide Médicale de l'Etat, AME)
